summary:
# NOTES: "THE POMP OF YESTERDAY" by Joseph Hocking (WWI story)

**Front matter:** Epigraph Kipling "Recessional" (Lest we forget). Foreword (March 1918): asks "Why is Victory delayed?"; statements came from informed sources; Somme descriptions from witnesses; author revisited front; finished Aug 1917; Russia chaos anticipated.

## CHAPTERS I–II (Plymouth, spring 1915)
- Narrator: Captain Luscombe (Cornish, recruiter, commissioned by War Office; ex-Volunteers officer; ~40, "old" to girl; Cornishman, loves Cornwall).
- Plymouth Harbour: amnesiac man from India (came via Bombay, scars, Indians with knives in dreams, L5 notes in vest). Named **Paul Edgecumbe** (after Mount Edgecumbe; Paul = scriptural character with strange experiences). Wears motley clothes; narrator buys clothes; hotel facing The Hoe.
- Edgecumbe returns salute to soldiers → likely soldier. Enlists at recruiting meeting in Plymouth hall (~2000 people); shouts "Join! how can a man, who is a man, do anything else?"
- Narrator summoned to Falmouth; can't find Edgecumbe.
- Months later, lunch with **Colonel Gray** (Exeter); **Sir Roger Granville** (chairman of Plymouth meeting; Granitelands, Devon; Granville family quarrel Cornwall/Devon). Roger romanticises the case.
- Roger's motor drive; Sir Richard Granville mention.

## CHAPTER III (Granitelands)
- **Norah Blackwater**: tall, ~25, furtive, engaged to Maurice St. Mabyn (killed in Egypt, Arab/mullah uprising) before he left; now loved by George.
- **Lorna Bolivick**: ~19–20, brown eyes, childlike, impetuous, "ugly as sin" (her claim); father "dad" named her after Blackmore's Lorna Doone; brothers at war. Lorna Bolivick is the ideal for Edgecumbe.
- **George St. Mabyn**: ~28, captain Territorials, wounded at Ypres, now squire of St. Mabyn house, deeply in love with Norah; haunted look when Edgecumbe story told.
- Lorna insists narrator must find Edgecumbe. Narrator promises (written in diary, May 29, witnessed by Lorna: "Witnessed by Lorna Bolivick, Bolivick, South Petherwin").
- Narrator suspicious of George.

## CHAPTER IV (St. Mabyn house)
- **Captain Horace Springfield**: tall, dark, lean, 30–35, grey streaks, deep-set eyes, scar on cheek below right temple (right ear in later chapters), receding forehead; served Egypt and India; Maurice's "pal"; claims Maurice died in skirmish in Egypt (mullah, Upper Egypt) after he was with him.
- Lorna: Norah "snakes" – Springfield reminds Lorna of snakes. Lorna's home: Bolivick, near South Petherwin, ~5 miles away.
- Narrator sees George and Springfield conspire; Springfield and George use Christian names.

## CHAPTER V (Raid, miracle)
- Narrator's raid, Feb-ish 1916 (winter 1915–16), near front; 20 men; captured with Sergeant Smith; German cave/dug-out; German captain "Better put a bullet into their brains."
- Bombardment; Edgecumbe (as English prisoner, in Tommy uniform) persuades ~30 Germans to surrender ("Isle of Wight," "picnic"). Leads them to British lines. Narrator identifies him.
- Footnote: incident told by a British officer, true.

## CHAPTER VI (Memory)
- Edgecumbe saluted narrator. Colonel congratulates. Edgecumbe: no memory; trained at Exeter, Swindon, Bramshott, Salisbury Plain; declines commission; knows German/French, mathematics now.
- Narrator tests names: Devonshire, Granitelands, Maurice St. Mabyn, Norah Blackwater, Springfield (Edgecumbe describes Springfield's face; feels dislike).
- Colonel reports Edgecumbe missing (German raid).

## CHAPTER VII (Cause of failure)
- Edgecumbe found alive, wounded arm (sprained in quarry; drugged Germans with ether). He gives speech: drink in munitions works (fireman delayed Boat 24 hours; Government allowed public-houses); munitions wasted; "man-power"; sugar/grain used for drink; King, Kitchener, Chancellor signed pledge.
- **Major George St. Mabyn** enters; he and Springfield now both at front; St. Mabyn startled by Edgecumbe. Edgecumbe is "D.C.L.I." Private.

## CHAPTER VIII (Eavesdropper)
- St. Mabyn announces engagement to Norah (not public). Invites narrator to billet at St. Pinto.
- Narrator at St. Pinto; hears George and Springfield in copse: plot to make Edgecumbe "never go back to England alive"; "Are you sure Luscombe has no suspicions?"; Springfield: "foul play". Edgecumbe had visited their billet ~ before.
- Letter from George inviting narrator to dinner Thursday.

## CHAPTER IX (Missing)
- Dinner at St. Pinto; Springfield's probing; narrator followed. Edgecumbe waiting at billet; narrator says nothing yet; Edgecumbe leaves midnight; angry voices + pistol shot; Edgecumbe missing.

## CHAPTER X (Trenches, Somme prep)
- End May 1916; narrator given job 5 miles south.
- Lorna's letter (June): wants Edgecumbe's photo; "Captain Luscombe … you're old"; her wounded Tommy with no legs asks for patent-leather dancing shoes. Narrator sends photo (taken by comrade amateur).
- 1 July: Somme attack; narrator north of Ancre; Germans counter; narrator fights three Germans with rifle; Edgecumbe rescues him ("This is twice you've saved my life"). Edgecumbe: "I have found more than life." Joy in his eyes.

## CHAPTER XI (Edgecumbe's story)
- Narrator's colonel; M.O.; Thiepval not taken.
- Edgecumbe's story: rescued from quarry by old man with cart; statement tallied with narrator's; attended Y.M.C.A. hut; speaker (unnamed) made him realise God; read New Testament; "Christ"; "Sermon on the Mount".
- Cry heard (Indian vendetta cry); Springfield's voice → Edgecumbe: "I know that voice!"; loathing.
- Lorna letter: photo; "eyes reading my soul"; "bring him to see me."

## CHAPTER XII (Somme struggle)
- Late July near Montauban; narrator shell-shocked, buried; Edgecumbe digging out Springfield (buried). Corporal Wilkins witnessed. Doctor: Springfield "may pull through"; Edgecumbe "miracle", back to duty.
- Colonel Gray (Edgecumbe's colonel): recommend decoration. Narrator sent to England. On boat, Edgecumbe: "I have great things to tell you."

## CHAPTER XIII (Madness / Christianity)
- Edgecumbe's conversion: prayer; Sermon on Mount; "war by love"; "God won't do for us what we can do for ourselves"; Tommy fatalist; Cromwell comparison; Victor Hugo (Waterloo, God against Napoleon); Germans "Lord, Lord".
- "If God is not with us we are lost."

## CHAPTER XIV (Logic)
- Drink and impurity; Lloyd George's quote; Edgecumbe's argument: victory at cost of souls = lose; abstainers as brave; Admiral Beatty and Sir William Robertson quotes ("Make the men religious, Bishop"; "Not by might, nor by power…" Zechariah 4:6).
- Lorna's letter: "I shall take no refusal"; invites both to Bolivick.
- Edgecumbe agrees to go.

## CHAPTER XV (Devonshire)
- Narrator & Edgecumbe train via Exeter; **Colonel Heywood** (C.O., OTC): Edgecumbe is artillery officer, genius at gunnery; Heywood will check Indian Army missing officers.
- South Petherwin station; carriage; Bolivick: granite gateposts. Edgecumbe stares at Lorna; burning eyes.

## CHAPTER XVI (Bolivick)
- **Sir Thomas Bolivick** (baronet, hearty, West Country). **Lady Bolivick**. Two Bolivick sons at front (Tom, another).
- Edgecumbe: "I have [seen you] in my dreams"; first time spoke to woman.
- Dinner: Norah Blackwater present. Narrator tells Thirty-Germans story; Sir Thomas shakes Edgecumbe's hand.
- Springfield and **Charlie Buller** arrive (Lady Bolivick: Buller invited; Lorna flushes).

## CHAPTER XVII (New development)
- **Charlie Buller**: 24, first lieutenant Devonshire Yeomanry, wounded, suitor for Lorna; estate joins Bolivick. Norah: "as good as settled."
- Springfield's face pale, scar pronounced; Buller under his sway.
- Narrator tells the rescue story; Springfield asks "who?" – Springfield thanks Edgecumbe ("you saved my life").
- Edgecumbe in narrator's room: "I am in love"; "that man… I know him"; "serpent"; "Indian cry… vengeance".

## CHAPTER XVIII (Tragic happening)
- Edgecumbe: "God never makes a mistake"; vows.
- Next day (Saturday) Lorna: "I am disappointed in your friend."; Springfield & Buller lunch.
- Evening: Edgecumbe collapses ("like one dead").

## CHAPTER XIX (Mysterious illness)
- **Dr. Merril** (country doctor, South Petherwin): suspects poison; no motor chauffeur; Sir Thomas's car; Springfield offers to drive; narrator goes to Plymouth with **Buller** as guide (Buller can't drive, left leg weak).
- Narrator asks Merril to keep room closed.

## CHAPTER XX (Strange night)
- **Colonel McClure** (chief St George's Military Hospital, Plymouth; 12 years India). Drives back with narrator; examines.
- Springfield left about midnight (Sir Thomas). Springfield took Buller's car; Buller says Springfield "heir to peerage" via **St. Mabyn**; Springfield "poor as church mouse."
- Lorna still up; Sir Thomas thinks Edgecumbe dying.

## CHAPTER XXI (McClure's verdict)
- Blue spot on left arm (below elbow), discoloration; McClure injects antidote (Indian poison); Edgecumbe revives.
- McClure: "some one poisoned him"; narrator tells suspicions to McClure privately.

## CHAPTER XXII (Edgecumbe's resolve)
- Edgecumbe awake; in love; "I mean to marry her." Narrator objects (no money, possible wife).
- Springfield & Buller lunch; Springfield with Lorna.

## CHAPTER XXIII (Springfield's progress)
- Narrator questions Springfield about India, poison; Springfield's cigarette; "Edgecumbe is a bounder."
- Springfield's lunch; Sir Thomas: Springfield heir to **Lord Carbis** (brewer peer, created 1890; Carbis Castle; ~£1 million estates).
- McClure: "guard him as if he were your own son."
- Edgecumbe: will propose to Lorna.

## CHAPTER XXIV (Strange love-making)
- Autumn walk; Edgecumbe proposes; Lorna refuses ("I never loved you… Springfield").
- Edgecumbe's dinner humour; Sir Thomas: "fellow is a genius."
- Return to London next day.

## CHAPTER XXV (Why is victory delayed?)
- Train from Bristol; Somme winter pause; Edgecumbe: "Where does God come in?"; Kipling Recessional; Admiral Beatty; "Germany's atheism" argument.
- Edgecumbe heads to London to study it.
- Paddington: Springfield appears.

## CHAPTER XXVI (Where does God come in?)
- Springfield invites them to club; apologises to Edgecumbe; offers to show London.
- Edgecumbe at Y.M.C.A. hut (officers' hostel), poisoned relapse; narrator moves to hotel.
- Visit House of Commons; **Cabinet Minister** (old friend of narrator; golf); Edgecumbe: "Where does God come in?"; drink and Lloyd George 1915 quote.
- Waterloo station troop arrivals.

## CHAPTER XXVII (Seeing London)
- Waterloo station Y.M.C.A. welcomes; vice preyers.
- Music-hall revue (vulgar); tea hotel; Piccadilly, Haymarket, Pall Mall; Edgecumbe: "is the life-blood pure?"

## CHAPTER XXVIII (Sunshine and shadow)
- Churches; sermon "they that were ready went into the marriage feast"; hospital for venereal disease; Crystal Palace sailors.
- Dinner: Sir Thomas, Lady Bolivick, Lorna with Springfield at another table; Edgecumbe: "a battle royal… to save a woman's soul."

## CHAPTER XXIX (Cross currents)
- Springfield now **Colonel** (gazetted; battalion on return). Narrator and Lorna: "Am I to congratulate you?" – Lorna: "not yet".
- Springfield, drunk, insinuates Edgecumbe criminal madman.
- Edgecumbe: will fight drink; Admiral Beatty again; "not ready for victory"; Russia.

## CHAPTER XXX (March of events, 1917)
- Narrator writing as diary-like account; Sir Roger's earlier interest.
- Edgecumbe letters: promoted lieutenant→captain; greatest artillery officer; "God is speaking".
- German unrestricted sub warfare Feb 1; food crisis; Russian Revolution; US declares war; Wilson speech; "Romanoffs' pomp… dream of yesterday".
- June 1917: Edgecumbe appears at training camp, left arm sling.

## CHAPTER XXXI (Edgecumbe's return)
- Edgecumbe: Springfield and St. Mabyn both at Vimy, Ypres, Messines; Springfield tried to frame him as German spy (officer in Berlin); Edgecumbe's "little stunt" (scheme with General D.H.Q.); Military Cross → will get **D.S.O.**
- Edgecumbe still seeks Lorna; "God has decreed"; Times article praising him.

## CHAPTER XXXII (Great meeting)
- National Hotel, London. Meeting on drink & impurity: Cabinet Minister, General; Edgecumbe in uniform (major) speaks; "Drink and Impurity"; "blood-red crime"; "I will make no terms"; "God lives… Czars… Kaiser"; crowd frenzy; chairman identifies Major Edgecumbe. Old clergyman prays. General: "worth more than an army corps."

## CHAPTER XXXIII (The lifted curtain)
- Telegram from Bolivick. Springfield, St. Mabyn present; Lorna in nurse's uniform. Lord Carbis coming (surprise: engagement?).
- Edgecumbe: doctor (Harley Street nerve specialist) said vivid event may pierce amnesia; "sixth sense".
- Edgecumbe tells George: "Maurice… he's not dead."
- **Lord and Lady Carbis** arrive: "John!… Jack, our Jack!" Edgecumbe = **Jack Carbis**, their son. Faints.

## CHAPTER XXXIV (Memory)
- Lorna checks heartbeat; Lord Carbis (had news of son's death in India; death notice paper). Edgecumbe: "The mists, the cobwebs, the black curtain" gone.
- Dinner; Lady Bolivick; Springfield: Jack will drop fortune.
- Lorna: "Hope you don't."
- Jack: "come to library."

## CHAPTER XXXV (Afterwards)
- Library: Jack recovers; "Mother"; fear of relapse; Dr. Merril checks.

## CHAPTER XXXVI (Edgecumbe's resolution)
- Next morning, Jack well; "one black ugly spot".
- Narrator's worries: Jack's refusal of drink money; Springfield's attention to Lorna.
- Narrator & Lorna: "I shall marry Colonel Springfield, if—". Lorna: "Paul Edgecumbe nicer name".
- Jack refuses drink money; "I am a poor man with nothing but my pay"; Springfield "still means to have her".

## CHAPTER XXXVII (Maurice St. Mabyn)
- Jack relates Maurice's story: Maurice in India/Bizna July 1914; Springfield attacked him (stabbed, left for dead); Maurice reported to **General Gregory** (died 2 years ago, "remain dead"); blackmail; Maurice's servant; attacked; tortured by Turks/Afghan; amnesia.

## CHAPTER XXXVIII (A bombshell)
- Family dinner (Lord & Lady Carbis leaving next day; George, Springfield, Norah present). Jack reveals Maurice alive; accuses Springfield; Springfield denies, asks Lorna to marry him publicly.

## CHAPTER XXXIX (Springfield at bay)
- Lorna silent; Jack: "to save Miss Bolivick". Springfield denies; "Gregory died".
- **Maurice St. Mabyn** enters, alive; "Maurice!" (George). Contempt in Maurice's eyes; orders Springfield gone; Lorna looks at Springfield then leaves room. Springfield exits.

## CHAPTER XL (Maurice's generosity)
- Maurice forgives George; cold to Norah (who loves Maurice, lost him). Jack & Maurice talk.
- Narrator & Lorna at rose garden: "I never loved him… I shall never marry him."
- Sir Thomas: **Springfield found dead in Plymouth hotel (poison, Indian, suicide)**; Lorna looks relieved.
- Narrator takes Lorna to station.

## CHAPTER XLI (The new hope)
- Springfield's letter: "Life's not worth living"; "great secret"; sealed package ("not to be opened within a week of my burial").
- Lorna's letter (Aug): brother Tom; invites narrator.
- Jack meets narrator at station; motor; Jack's views: England's spiritual change; "mills of God grind slowly".
- Jack says Lorna will come to him "in this world or next".

## CHAPTER XLII (An unfinished story)
- Narrator to Bolivick. Lorna reveals Springfield had threatened to expose Jack's Indian "deeds" unless she married him; she was afraid; she loves Jack.
- Jack arrives (motored 150 miles); Lorna and Jack walk; narrator: "this morning you called me brother".
- Jack goes to "beard the lion" (Sir Thomas). End. Narrator: "Lorna is to be my sister" (kisses).
